items.entity: volume fraction Vf of the cantilever topology optimization
items.description: Sec. 2.1/Fig. 2 show three runs (Fig. 2b Vf=0.7, 2c Vf=0.5, 2d Vf=0.3) without naming a reference case. For the same cantilever, the Sec. 4.1 text says Vf=0.5, which matches V=0.5·V̄=3900 cm³ (150×52×1) and the Fig. 4/18 captions. The Fig. 12 caption for the same problem says Vf=0.3.
readings: Vf = 0.5 (Sec. 4.1 text, Figs. 4 and 18, 3900 cm³)
Vf = 0.3 (Fig. 12 caption, Fig. 2d)
Vf = 0.7 (Fig. 2b)

items.entity: point load F = 100 kN on the free end
items.description: Sec. 2.1 and Sec. 4.1 give the magnitude and the position (18 cm below the top edge, on the end opposite the support) but never the direction. The direction is shown only in Fig. 2a/Fig. 12. Indirect hints: Sec. 4.1 does a vertical deflection check and uses the sign convention 'vertical downward deflection – positive'.
readings: vertical, downward (-y)
vertical, upward (+y): same minimum-compliance layout as downward
horizontal, in-plane along the span (axial)

items.description: Sec. 2.1 says only 'one edge of the domain is fixed' and Sec. 4.1 says 'One face of the plate is fixed', with the load on 'the opposite free end'. Which of the two 52 cm edges is clamped is visible only in Fig. 2a/12. The Fig. 4/18 captions (tagged 'left mid' / 'left top and bottom' boundary pixels) suggest the left edge.
readings: entire left 52 cm edge (x = 0) clamped (ux = uy = 0), load on the right edge (x = 150 cm)
entire right 52 cm edge clamped, load on the left edge (mirror image of the first reading, same compliance)

items.description: Sec. 1.3.1 says the domain is discretized with 'a structured grid and hexahedral linear elements'. Sec. 4.1 says '150 × 52 × 1 linear quadrilateral elements' for this cantilever. Neither section says whether a 2D model is plane stress or plane strain.
readings: 2D 4-node bilinear quadrilaterals, plane stress, thickness 1 cm
2D 4-node bilinear quadrilaterals, plane strain
3D 8-node trilinear hexahedra, a single layer through the 1 cm thickness (150 × 52 × 1)

items.entity: grid resolution for the Fig. 2 runs
items.description: Sec. 2.1 gives no discretization, even though it says 'different mesh sizes can vary these outputs'. The only grid given is in Sec. 4.1 (150 × 52 × 1, i.e. 1 cm × 1 cm elements) for the Vf = 0.5 run. Nothing confirms the Vf = 0.7 and 0.3 runs of Fig. 2 used the same grid.
readings: 150 × 52 elements of 1 cm × 1 cm (as in Sec. 4.1)
a different grid for the Fig. 2 runs, e.g. 300 × 104 elements of 0.5 cm

items.description: R = 1.2 (Fig. 2 caption, Sec. 4.1) has no unit. The geometry is given in cm, the material in N/mm², and Eq. 7 uses the centre-to-centre distance between elements. On a 1 cm grid, element units and cm give the same filter; with any other unit or grid they differ.
readings: 1.2 element widths (= 1.2 cm on the 150 × 52 grid; only the 4 edge-adjacent neighbours get weight 0.2)
1.2 cm physical length, kept fixed if the grid changes
1.2 mm (smaller than one element, so effectively no filtering)

items.entity: filtering scheme / density used in SIMP interpolation
items.description: Sec. 1.3.1 says the densities are filtered and the filtered densities replace ρ in Eqs. 1–4, which describes a density filter. But Eq. 6 as printed has ρ_i rather than ρ_j in the numerator, which makes the filter an identity, and Eqs. 11/13 use the unfiltered ρ_j in the penalization derivative. So it is unclear whether a density filter or a sensitivity filter was used, and which density drives the stiffness and the volume.
readings: density filter ρ̂_i = Σ_j H_ij v_j ρ_j / Σ_j H_ij v_j, with E(ρ̂) in stiffness and volume and chain-rule sensitivities
sensitivity filter (Sigmund-type) applied to ∂C/∂ρ, with stiffness and volume from the unfiltered ρ

items.entity: design-update algorithm for the topology optimization
items.description: Sec. 1.3.1 says only 'gradient-based optimization'. No optimizer, move limit or damping is given for the topology stage. MMA and SQP are named only for the frame size/layout stage (Sec. 2.4, Table 1).
readings: Optimality Criteria update (move limit 0.2, damping exponent 0.5, bisection on the volume multiplier)
MMA with standard parameters

items.description: Only 'Maximum iterations = 200' is given (Fig. 2 caption, Sec. 4.1). No tolerance on density or compliance change is given; the 1e-4 tolerances in Table 1 apply to the frame optimization. The convergence history in Fig. 13 cannot be seen.
readings: run all 200 iterations
stop when max |Δρ| < 0.01, capped at 200 iterations
stop when relative compliance change < 1e-4, capped at 200 iterations

items.description: The starting design for the topology optimization is not stated anywhere in Sec. 1.3.1, 2.1 or 4.1.
readings: uniform ρ = Vf in all elements
uniform ρ = 1 (fully solid start)

items.entity: plate thickness used in the topology-optimization model
items.description: Sec. 2.1 and Sec. 4.1 state the 1 cm thickness only 'for size optimization'. For the topology optimization the thickness is only implied by the '150 × 52 × 1' element count. In plane stress the thickness only scales the stiffness.
readings: 1 cm
unit thickness in the solver's unit system (e.g. 1 mm when working in N–mm)

items.entity: elements at the load point and along the fixed edge
items.description: Sec. 2.1 mentions no non-design regions. Sec. 4.1 says 'Fixed-end boundary pixels and force-applied pixels were tagged so no alteration is allowed during any stages of optimization'. This could mean these elements are held solid during the topology optimization, or only that they are protected during skeletonization and frame size/layout optimization.
readings: no passive elements; the whole 150 × 52 cm rectangle is designable
element(s) at the load point fixed solid (ρ = 1)
load-point element(s) plus the column of elements along the fixed edge fixed solid
